16.t: Working with data: diameter, myelin and speed
q: Calculate the increase in speed per micrometre of diameter for myelinated fibres.
Compare the effect of diameter on speed in myelinated and unmyelinated fibres.
Speed rises with diameter in both, but much more steeply with myelin: at 10 µm, 60 against 3.2 m s⁻¹ (about 19 times faster).
Estimate the diameter of a myelinated fibre as fast as the squid giant axon. Comment on your answer.
About 4 µm: over 100 times thinner than the squid axon, so myelin gives speed while saving space.
Explain how myelin increases conduction speed.
Myelin insulates the axon, so depolarisation happens only at the nodes of Ranvier: the impulse jumps from node to node (saltatory conduction).
